The study by Toyoda H, Kumada T, Tada T, et al., published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2017, evaluated the safety and efficacy of dual direct-acting antiviral therapy using daclatasvir and asunaprevir in elderly patients infected with hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1b. The findings demonstrated the effectiveness of this regimen in this specific patient population. 2. Toyoda H, Kumada T, Tada T, et al., in their 2016 study published in the Journal of Gastroenterology, investigated the use of daclatasvir and asunaprevir in patients with chronic HCV genotype 1 infection undergoing hemodialysis. The study highlighted the safety and efficacy of this treatment approach in this challenging clinical scenario. 3. Toyota J, Karino Y, Suzuki F, et al., in a 2017 publication in the Journal of Gastroenterology, examined the fixed-dose combination of daclatasvir, asunaprevir, and beclabuvir in Japanese patients with HCV genotype 1 infection. The study provided evidence supporting the use of this combination therapy in this patient group. 4. Vermehren J, Athmann C, Gunther R, et al., in a study presented in the Journal of Hepatology in 2017, explored the use of a 6 million viral load cut-off to guide treatment duration with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir in patients with chronic HCV genotype 1 infection. The results were derived from the German Hepatitis C Registry (DHC-R). 5. Hyland R, Brainard D, Welzel TM, et al., in a 2017 study published in the Journal of Clinical Virology, compared on-treatment HCV RNA levels during direct-acting antiviral therapy using two different COBAS TaqMan HCV assays. The study provided insights into the performance of these diagnostic tools. 6. Vierling JM, Kugelmas M, Lawitz E, et al., in a 2015 study published in the Journal of Hepatology, assessed the efficacy of an 8-week regimen of grazoprevir plus elbasvir, with and without ribavirin, in treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic patients with HCV genotype 1b infection. The findings supported the use of this short-duration therapy in this patient population. 7. Wei L, Burnevich E, Sheen IS, et al., in a phase III randomized multinational clinical trial (CCORAL) presented in Hepatology International in 2017, evaluated the efficacy and safety of elbasvir/grazoprevir in treatment-naive subjects with chronic HCV genotypes 1, 4, and 6 infections. The study demonstrated the effectiveness of this regimen across diverse genotypes. 8. Wei L, Hou J, Luo Y, et al., in the ONYX-I study presented in Hepatology International in 2017, investigated the safety and efficacy of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir in Asian adults with genotype 1b chronic HCV infection. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study provided robust evidence for the use of this regimen in this population. 9. Wei L, Xie Q, Hou J, et al., in a phase III study conducted in China and presented in Hepatology International in 2017, evaluated the combination of sofosbuvir, ribavirin, and pegylated interferon in patients with HCV genotypes 1, 2, 3, or 6 infections. The study highlighted the efficacy of this regimen in a diverse patient population. 10. Wei L, Zhang M, Xu M, et al., in a phase III open-label study published in the Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2016, assessed the combination of daclatasvir and asunaprevir in Asian patients with chronic HCV genotype 1b infection who were ineligible for or intolerant to interferon alfa therapies, with or without ribavirin. The study demonstrated the utility of this regimen in this specific patient group. 11. Younossi Z, Stepanova M, Han KH, et al., in a 2016 study published in the Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, reported that Asian patients with HCV genotype 1 treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir experienced high efficacy and significant improvements in health-related quality of life (HRQoL). 12. Younossi ZM, Stepanova M, Charlton M, et al., in a 2016 study published in The Lancet Gastroenterology and Hepatology, analyzed patient-reported outcomes with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, with or without ribavirin, in patients with HCV-related decompensated cirrhosis. The findings were derived from the randomized, open-label ASTRAL-4 phase III trial. 13. Younossi ZM, Stepanova M, Sulkowski M, et al., in a 2016 study published in Clinical Infectious Diseases, demonstrated that a ribavirin-free regimen with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir was associated with high efficacy and improved patient-reported outcomes in patients with genotypes 2 and 3 chronic HCV. The results were based on the ASTRAL-2 and -3 clinical trials. 14. Zeuzem S, Dusheiko GM, Salupere R, et al., in a 2014 study published in the New England Journal of Medicine, evaluated the combination of sofosbuvir and ribavirin in patients with HCV genotypes 2 and 3. The study provided evidence supporting the use of this regimen in these genotypes. 15. Zeuzem S, Flamm SL, Tong MJ, et al., in the POLARIS-4 study presented in Hepatology in 2016, investigated the efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir for 12 weeks in direct-acting antiviral-experienced patients with HCV genotypes 1-6 infections. The study highlighted the effectiveness of these regimens in this challenging patient population.
